summary: tab visibility + network switch during streaming leads to duplicate last-chunk and suppressed terminal event on client
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when users switch networks while a streaming session is active and the browser tab is backgrounded (tab visibility hidden + network change cellular->wifi), the last token chunk is delivered twice with non-monotonic choice indexes and the client's final "end"/terminal event is not processed, resulting in truncated final output.

Impact: Reproducible for ~30% of sessions for a single Acme Health integration. Truncated outputs are causing incorrect clinical note completions in their product workflow. Affects production traffic in us-east region.

Environment: Acme Health production integration (enterprise account), browser: Chrome 111 on Android 14 (reported), client uses our JS SDK 2.3.1 with SSE fallback to WebSocket enabled in their config.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start a long streaming generation (approx 600-1200 tokens).
2) Put the tab into background (visibilitychange = hidden).
3) Trigger a network change (turn mobile data off and back on or move into Wi-Fi).
4) Tab comes back to foreground and client reconnects.

Expected behavior: Client reconnect/resume should stitch the stream and preserve a single terminal event indicating completion of the choice.

Actual behavior: Customer observes duplicate last-chunk content (same tokens repeated) and, in ~30% of reproductions, the client-side code does not receive the terminal/end event so the UI shows a partial sentence with no completion marker. The repeated chunk has an older timestamp/choice index that precedes the already-processed last chunk, which appears to trigger client dedup logic and causes the client to ignore the subsequent end event.

Logs/Attachments: Customer provided HARs, SDK logs, and a short recording (attached). Sample server-side stream metadata extracted from trace: "x-session-id: 0a7f3e", "stream-choice-index: 42", "event-ts: 2026-03-10T18:22:03.123Z" followed by a duplicate fragment with "stream-choice-index: 41" and event-ts 2026-03-10T18:22:02.987Z.

Notes: Customer is on an enterprise SLA and requests a mitigation while engineering investigates a permanent fix.

investigation_notes: Reproduction: Emulated network switch by toggling system network; reproduced ~60% of runs when tab was backgrounded and reconnect occurred within 5s.

Edge behavior: Fastly/CloudFront layer shows upstream connection reuse and a sequence where buffered trailing chunk is replayed after handshake, producing non-monotonic 'stream-choice-index' values in logs.

TLS logs: Brief TLS renegotiation and new TCP 0-RTT style resume observed; server emitted the last chunk before EOF, then edge replayed a buffered pre-reconnect frame resulting in duplicate content with older timestamp.

Client SDK: Current dedup logic drops fragments with lower-or-equal 'stream-choice-index' and assumes later fragments contain end flag. In duplicate case, the older fragment causes subsequent end event to be ignored due to race in dedup ordering.

Hypothesis: Combination of tab-visibility lifecycle on mobile (suspended JS timers), network switch at edge, and HTTP/2/connection reuse is causing reordering of final fragments. The client dedup logic and reliance on 'stream-choice-index' monotonicity amplifies the symptom.

Temporary mitigation idea: Make terminal/end event strongest signal; accept small duplicate token runs rather than dropping end notifications. Server-side could also attach per-event monotonic counter and an explicit 'final_event_id' to avoid ambiguity.
Telemetry: Instrumented extra tracing to capture 'event-seq' and TLS session id at the edge to correlate with customer IDs for further repro steps.
Related: linked to SUP-220501 (edge probe teardown suppressed terminal SSE event) as a potentially related edge-layer replay behavior
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 - Temporary mitigation shipped to customer: SDK 2.3.2-beta that prioritizes terminal/end flag over strict monotonic index when deciding to ignore an incoming end event. Customer smoke tests show reduction in truncated outputs.

Engineering action items: 1) Add server-side per-event monotonic counter and explicit final_event_id header (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/983). 2) Edge config change to disable replay of buffered stream frames across TLS renegotiation for streaming endpoints (config ticket INT-441).
Planned rollout: Server change in staged rollout to dedicated/canary pool for 48h, then global. Edge config change requires coordination with CDN provider and ops window (ETA 2026-03-20).

Follow-ups: Update JS SDK dedup docs and add integration test for backgrounded-tab + network-switch scenario. Notify client after full rollout and close ticket once confirmed by customer and telemetry shows <0.1% occurrence.
Workaround for customer until full fix: use SDK 2.3.2-beta or disable SSE->WebSocket fallback in their integration to avoid path that triggers edge replay in their environment.
